newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - P&O H1 will be reminder of problems.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - P&O H1 will be reminder of problems.

text.p: P&O which won back favour with the London stockmarket this week will remind investors of the difficulties being experienced in many parts of the group when it reports first-half results next Tuesday.

Analysts have few illusions that this year's cut-throat competition between ferries and Eurotunnel's channel tunnel will seriously dent operating profits, and say this and wider shipping weakness will offset a good half for cruises.
Forecasts in a fairly tight range between 115 and 118 million stg gave an average expectation of pretax profit of 115.75 million stg, down from last year's 131.9 million stg.

Despite the likely disappointment of the headline number, and bad news from non-cruise shipping markets, analysts said they saw the outlook brightening for P&O since its decision on September 9 to shift its container interests into a separate, joint venture company with Dutch group Nedlloyd NV.
The share price has recovered strongly from its long-term lows revisited earlier this summer and is already back near its year-high of just under 600p, from 517p a week ago.
UBS analyst Richard Hannah said he hoped P&O had listened to this reaction of shareholders to the Nedlloyd move "and this will give them an incentive to get on with other problem areas".

All analysts contacted by Reuters expect an interim dividend of 13.5 pence, as last year, and many saw a mounting expectation among investors, already being reflected in the price, that P&O will soon strike a deal to salvage profitability at its ferries.

Credit Lyonnais analyst Selwyn Jones said the seasonality of the key English Channel ferry market gave P&O some breathing space to find a deal, preferably with its leading rival Stena Line AB of Sweden, some time before next spring.

"It doesn't matter if the deal comes in the fourth quarter of this year or the first quarter of 1997 -- the view is just that some sort of collaboration should be in place by the start of the peak season," Jones said.

Analysts speculate that a deal that allows two or more of the ferry companies to rationalise ferry capacity and sailings, and firm up ticket prices from their current deeply-discounted levels, could salvage operating profits for P&O in the order of perhaps 50 million stg a year, or more.

As the company's share price charts its way back beyond 600p, the analysts warned that unless P&O can send a clear signal that a lifeboat is on the way for its ferries, investors may lose their nerve again and tip the stock back overboard.
